flow_ref: User story (not in any OCMS flow deck)
code_summary: ocmsadminprivateapi framework/workflows/furnish_processing/helpers/FurnishApprovalHelper (6 validation checks, addFurnishedOffender, changeProcessingStage), crud/beans/SystemConstant.FurnishStage, framework/workflows/agencies/toppan/upload/{helpers/ToppanUploadHelper (resolveStageContext, ocms_stage_map), models/ToppanStage}, framework/schedulers/ToppanUploadJobsScheduler, framework/controllers/ToppanUnifiedController. ocmsadminapi workflows/furnish/{stafffurnish/services/StaffFurnishService, manualreview/services/ManualReviewService}, crud/ocmsizdb/OcmsChangeOfProcessing/{EligibilityService, ChangeOfProcessingController}. ocmsadminui, ocmseserviceapi, ocmseserviceui, thirdpartyapi: no composition-vs-court decision code
note: Status in stories.json: Requirement given - Gen flow; demo_remark: 'Removed from demo list. Unable to verify.' There is no flow deck, so Sesuai means the code follows the story text. The core of the story, an automatic decision to offer composition or charge in court from conditions such as the count of the same offence under the driver's ID, is not in the code: there is no offence-history count per ID, no decision rule or flag, and Appendix B of Annex 1A is not in the repo (synonym greps over the six repos are empty; the only hit is the UI label 'Case Charge in Court' in ocmsadminui/src/components/datagrid/column/index.tsx:292). What exists is a fixed path: an approved driver furnish (automatic through Furnish Processing or manual through the staff portal) always goes to DN1 at the composition amount, then climbs DN1 -> DN2 -> DR3 -> CPC through ocms_stage_map. Letter generation only runs through the manual trigger because executeJob() in the day-end scheduler is commented out (ToppanUploadJobsScheduler.java:118). Ticket: OCMS-DF-2026-170 (Closed, Prod deployed) for resetting admin fee and amount_payable when a notice is redirected to DN1/RD1. The content of ocms_stage_map in the DB and the content of Appendix B cannot be verified from the repo.
recommendation: Do not claim as done. Only the precondition (a driver furnish goes to DN1 at the composition amount) and the fixed stage ladder exist; the composition-vs-court decision based on offence history is not built. Ask URA for Appendix B of Annex 1A and confirm whether this rule is built in another repo or still has to be built.

steps.step: The driver particulars furnished by the owner/hirer are received and the driver is recorded as the current offender
steps.detail: The Furnish Processing job runs in the syncinternetintranet scheduler every 10 minutes (enabled=true, cron-schedules-prod.properties:305-312). Each submission goes through 6 validation checks: active PS, HST, FIN/Passport, furnishable stage, existing hirer/driver, prior submission (FurnishApprovalHelper.java:150-176). When they pass, the old offender is switched to N and the new driver is created with offender_indicator Y plus ID, name, tel no and email from the form (FurnishApprovalHelper.java:546-558), and the form address is saved as furnished_mail with letter_address Y (FurnishApprovalHelper.java:627-634). A submission that fails a check goes to manual review (TS-PDP). This is the precondition of the story, not the composition/court decision it asks for. The content of the eService form cannot be verified in this step.

steps.step: OCMS counts the history of the same offence under the driver's ID (count of same offence history)
steps.detail: Not found. Greps with synonyms (repeat offender, offence history, same offence, previous/prior offence, offence count, COUNT per id_no) over the six repos find no query or logic that counts other notices or offences under the driver's ID. The only count on this path is CHECK 6, which counts other furnish submissions on the same notice (FurnishApprovalHelper.java:426-440); that is furnish history per notice, not offence history per driver. No maintenance ticket mentions this feature.

steps.step: OCMS compares the result with the pre-defined conditions (Appendix B of Annex 1A) to decide composition or court
steps.detail: There is no rule table, properties, flag or class holding pre-defined conditions to choose composition or court. The nearest 'condition' is CHECK 4 furnishable stage, which only matches the last/next processing stage pair against a fixed list (SystemConstant.java:237-244, FurnishApprovalHelper.java:319-336) to decide whether a furnish is allowed, not to choose composition vs court. Appendix B of Annex 1A is not in the repo, so the real conditions cannot be verified from the repo.

steps.step: When the decision is composition: the driver notice moves to stage DN1 at the composition amount
steps.detail: Every approved driver furnish always changes the stage to DN1 (last and next = DN1), clears administration_fee and resets amount_payable to composition_amount (FurnishApprovalHelper.java:648-653, 668-676; OCMS-DF-2026-170, Closed, Prod deployed), then sets next_processing_date = max(notice date + 7 days, tomorrow) (FurnishApprovalHelper.java:678-684). The staff portal path is the same: ocmsadminapi StaffFurnishService.java:922-928 and ManualReviewService.java:886-894 also set DN1 for the driver. The result matches the 'offer composition' branch, but it is applied to every driver without a decision based on conditions. Sebagian.

steps.step: When the charge-in-court conditions are met: the notice is taken to the court stage
steps.detail: There is no path to court that is chosen by conditions. A driver only reaches CPC through the fixed ladder DN1 -> DN2 -> DR3 -> CPC: the next stage is read from ocms_stage_map and, when empty, falls back to CPC for RR3/DR3 (ToppanUploadHelper.java:1813-1821; ToppanStage.java:22-24), each step advancing after the letter of that stage is processed. Staff can move the stage manually through Change Processing Stage (ocmsadminapi EligibilityService.java:49 holds DRIVER_STAGES DN1, DN2, DR3, CPC; ChangeOfProcessingController.java:47), but that is a human decision. So 'charge in court based on history' is replaced by a time ladder. The content of ocms_stage_map in the DB cannot be verified from the repo.

steps.step: The follow-up action runs automatically along the automated processing workflow (Appendix B)
steps.detail: After entering DN1, the next action follows the stage: Toppan Upload processes DN1, DN2, DR3 in order (ToppanLettersGeneratorJob.java:151-176) and the stage advances through ocms_stage_map (ToppanUploadHelper.java:1813-1821). But in the day-end scheduler the call toppanLettersGeneratorService.executeJob() is commented out (ToppanUploadJobsScheduler.java:118), so letters only run through the manual trigger POST /toppan/generate-letters (ToppanUnifiedController.java:34-40). The real Appendix B workflow order cannot be verified from the repo. Sebagian.
